scope: Define the runtime-owner registry and the coverage-matrix row schema used by later SGC-02 units. This file does not assign retained concepts to owners, does not claim implementation coverage, and does not begin SGC-02B mapping.

owner_registry_rules.registry_role: The registry supplies stable owner identifiers that coverage rows may reference; it does not itself prove coverage or implementation.
owner_registry_rules.extension_rule: A later SGC unit may add an owner_id only when the retained source and exact canonical authority evidence identify that owner. Unknown or vague 'current owner' references must remain unresolved until evidence identifies the owner.
owner_registry_rules.no_duplicate_authority_rule: SGC records references to governing owners and must not recreate or override their mechanics, content, or authority ledgers.
owner_registry_rules.broad_name_rule: A program or owner namespace by itself is insufficient evidence that a retained concept is covered.

field_rules.concept_id: Use one stable project-local concept identifier. One retained concept may not silently appear as multiple independent authority rows.
field_rules.source_refs: Must contain at least one source_id from the frozen retained-source inventory.
field_rules.concept_kind: Must be exactly one allowed concept kind in this schema.
field_rules.disposition: Must be exactly one allowed disposition from SGC-DISPOSITION-EVIDENCE-001.
field_rules.owner_id: Use a registered owner_id when the disposition asserts an owner or destination. It may be null only when the selected disposition legitimately has no resolved owner, such as unresolved_owner_decision, intentionally_unsupported, explicitly_superseded, or provenance_only.
field_rules.evidence: Must satisfy the selected disposition's evidence contract and include exact canonical or retained-source support. Broad program names alone are insufficient.

disposition_owner_requirements.implemented: owner_id is required and evidence must locate the governed implementation for the specific concept.
disposition_owner_requirements.planned_owned_elsewhere: owner_id is required and evidence must identify the canonical approved planning/authority record for that destination.
disposition_owner_requirements.content_only: owner_id is required when a governed content owner/destination exists; evidence must state that no runtime implementation claim is made.
disposition_owner_requirements.explicitly_superseded: owner_id may be null; evidence must identify the superseding authority and rationale.
disposition_owner_requirements.intentionally_unsupported: owner_id may be null; evidence must identify the owner-approved/canonical unsupported decision and reason.
disposition_owner_requirements.unresolved_owner_decision: owner_id may be null; evidence must preserve the unresolved question and source conflict/gap without inventing an owner.
disposition_owner_requirements.provenance_only: owner_id may be null; evidence must state the provenance reason and that no implementation/content obligation is created.

validation_rules: Every source_ref resolves to the frozen retained-source inventory.
Every non-null owner_id resolves to runtime_owner_registry or a later evidence-backed registry extension.
Every disposition is allowed by SGC-DISPOSITION-EVIDENCE-001.
No row may claim implemented from a completed program name alone.
No missing definition, effect, amount, ownership, or other source fact may be fabricated to force a row closed.
ARI/SAA/P3D routes may not be silently dropped or misreported as implemented.
Duplicate authority and orphan-owner conditions are surfaced for SGC-02C rather than normalized away.

invariants: SGC-02A defines registry/schema only; SGC-02B performs core mechanics/rules/loop mapping.
The frozen retained-source inventory remains the only source-id universe for initial SGC coverage rows.
The owner registry is referential metadata, not a duplicate authority ledger.
Unknown owners remain explicit unresolved evidence gaps rather than invented registry entries.
Historical evidence cannot override newer canonical repository authority.
